key_insight: CommCP combines LLM-based inter-agent language reasoning with conformal prediction to calibrate uncertainty, enabling agents to communicate selectively — sending only low-confidence or critical information — which cuts communication overhead while preserving task success.
problem_solved: Efficient, reliable multi-robot coordination for language-specified manipulation tasks where heterogeneous agents must gather scene information and cooperate under limited communication bandwidth and uncalibrated LLM outputs.
method: Use LLMs as local communicative reasoning modules for question generation, scene-query answering, and plan proposals among heterogeneous robots.
Apply conformal prediction to calibrate LLM uncertainty and impose a selective-communication gate: only messages below a confidence threshold (or flagged as critical) are transmitted.
Coordinate task allocation and execution via a lightweight multi-agent protocol that leverages selective messages to synchronize actions while minimizing bandwidth.
impact: Enables scalable, bandwidth-efficient multi-robot deployments that leverage large language models safely by making their outputs reliability-aware; useful for practitioners building distributed robotic systems or multi-agent decision pipelines where communication cost and trust in LLM outputs matter.
visual_elements: System pipeline diagram: Human instruction → per-robot LLM reasoning → conformal prediction gate (calibration) → selective messages → coordinated action
Bar/line chart: message volume vs task success comparing naive broadcast, thresholded (CommCP), and no-communication baselines
Sequence diagram: example interaction showing when an agent queries, when conformal gate permits transmission, and how others react

paper_title: CommCP: Efficient Multi-Agent Coordination via LLM-Based Communication with Conformal Prediction
paper_authors: Xiaopan Zhang, Zejin Wang, Zhixu Li, Jianpeng Yao, Jiachen Li
